findings.title: Linux TSYNC propagates folder permissions without their Landlock boundary
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The seccomp forms that allow folder writes and the markers for Landlock must reach only threads that actually hold the matching Landlock policy.
findings.observed: The caller-only Landlock fallback sets LAYER, SCOPE and possibly FOLDERS. The same rules, including those bits and the folder-write seccomp forms, can be installed process-wide by seccomp TSYNC. Sibling entry subsequently interprets the copied marks as evidence of its own Landlock. This remains present after the mid-audit changes for skipping already-installed filters.
findings.impact: Sibling threads can receive the folder-write permissions without the path boundary. Reports on subsequent entry can also confirm a signal scope that did not reach that thread. The initial WholeProcess refusal does not revoke the peer's installed policy.
findings.recommendedFix: Keep per-thread Landlock provenance separate from filters, validate coverage before propagating the path-dependent policy, and fail closed when the Landlock boundary cannot be proved across the threads receiving the permissions.
findings.requiredVerification: Require a passing per-thread audit on ABI 6–7, on ABI 8 and when a host refuses Landlock TSYNC. Include folders, re-entry and independent evidence for each primitive.

findings.title: Concurrent Linux isolation calls race
findings.reproduction: Two threads call `enter_with(Options::new().all_threads())` and `enter_with_folders` at once.
findings.expected: One isolation of the process at a time.
findings.observed: Both read no layer and no filter; one call's empty layer, put on every thread, closed the folders the other granted while it reported `FolderWrites` Confirmed.
findings.impact: A false report, and folders closed under a program that was told they are open.
findings.recommendedFix: Serialize the critical section.
findings.requiredVerification: Source review of the guard; the fork case where another thread held it.

findings.title: Landlock TSYNC can replace a sibling's protection before seccomp refuses synchronization
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Previously installed protection should remain in force when strict admission fails, as the API guide promises.
findings.observed: Landlock ABI 8 applies the caller's domain to siblings. This can replace a sibling's stricter or different domain. Seccomp runs afterwards and can refuse a divergent filter tree. The implementation cannot roll back the already successful Landlock call. The technical guide mentions domain replacement, while the API's general promise also covers strict failure.
findings.impact: A sibling can be left with different path authority after the overall process-wide check fails. This applies to explicit multithreaded opt-in where differently sandboxed siblings coexist.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a controlled process with a common known starting policy or decline this combination. Define which operations can replace another thread's policy and what each failure leaves in force.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the policy of every thread after strict success and after a refused second primitive, including a host-supplied Landlock domain.

findings.title: Linux thread census can certify whole-process reach with a surviving sibling

evidence.challenge: A review correctly distinguished exiting after emission (which cannot yield a count of one) from exiting after the iterator takes its task reference but before it reads the PID. The latter branch skips emission, advances the index and ends the walk. A still-live leader does not prevent omission of a sibling.

findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Single-thread reach is reported only when the process really has one thread or the relevant policy is synchronized.
findings.observed: The kernel task directory iterator can skip an exiting entry before returning its name. If that task dies, its successor lookup can end the iteration. Directory position can advance even though the entry was omitted. A short successful listing can therefore leave a surviving sibling uncounted. The code trusts a count of one, skips TSYNC and marks the calling thread's filter process-wide. The same incomplete walk is trusted by traced(), so a skipped thread can also leave a tracer unreported.
findings.impact: A caller that explicitly requires process-wide measures can proceed on a false reach report. This predicate was present before TSYNC and now also decides whether an explicitly requested synchronization runs.
findings.recommendedFix: Use an authoritative kernel thread count for the single-thread path. Require synchronization or return unconfirmed reach where the applicable process scope cannot be established.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise reports during sibling exit and thread churn and confirm that any passing strict admission establishes the declared scope.

findings.title: macOS channel checks miss some writable shared file mappings
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: A complete inventory used by only() accounts for all writable shared mappings, including those whose original descriptor is closed.
findings.observed: XNU can report a singly mapped external object as SM_PRIVATE. Inheritance can be changed independently of shared backing. The two predicates used to identify a shared mapping therefore miss a writable mapping that remains shared with its backing file.
findings.impact: A clean channel report may leave a writable route to a file despite the descriptor check and the no-file-write policy for newly opened channels.
findings.recommendedFix: Treat ambiguous potentially writable file-backed mappings conservatively, or mark the inventory incomplete. Use the kernel view rather than fork-inheritance behavior alone to establish sharing.
findings.requiredVerification: Require a native macOS fixture that confirms a complete account of writable file mappings across descriptor closure, distinct inheritance settings and single versus multiple mappings.

findings.title: macOS folder privacy can ignore inherited ACL permissions
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: is_private() promises only the user can reach the folder when it returns true.
findings.observed: The flag is computed solely from st_mode in hold(). On macOS a directory can inherit extended ACL entries that grant access despite mode 0700.
findings.impact: Callers can place sensitive output in a folder that other identities can reach after receiving a positive privacy check.
findings.recommendedFix: Inspect effective ACLs on the held directory and default to unconfirmed where access exclusivity cannot be established, or narrow the API to report verified mode bits alone.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify native creation below restrictive and permissive inherited ACLs and distinguish filesystem permission support from privacy.

findings.title: Windows reports successful hidden input after failed console discards
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Input queued before the prompt and the unused end of a paste are discarded, or the function restores settings and returns an error.
findings.observed: FlushConsoleInputBuffer is called twice without checking its result. Its console handle must have GENERIC_WRITE. The read and mode checks can work with GENERIC_READ.
findings.impact: A valid read-oriented console handle can admit input that was queued or echoed before the hidden prompt. The suffix of a paste can reach the next reader.
findings.recommendedFix: Require a successful initial discard before reading. Surface an ending discard failure while still restoring mode, and maintain the documented behavior for redirected handles.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify on native Windows with console input handles of both access classes, queued input, cancellation and restore.

findings.title: Unix hidden input does not verify or report an incomplete restore and drain
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Restoration should verify the original terminal state, and input should be drained without waiting under verified hidden settings.
findings.observed: Startup checks tcsetattr with tcgetattr because a partial change can return success. Restore uses only the setter. It ignores failure to enter the drain mode, drain errors and exhaustion, and reads without checking that nonblocking drain attributes actually took effect.
findings.impact: After an apparently successful call the terminal may still be in a changed mode or leave input for the next reader. If the assumed drain mode did not apply, an attempted drain can wait for input.
findings.recommendedFix: Read back the changed fields before draining and after restoring. Always attempt the restore and return an error when the documented restore or discard could not be established. State any deliberate discard bound.
findings.requiredVerification: Validate successful and failed restoration with ordinary PTY fixtures and a controlled partial-change failure.

findings.title: Stack clearing does not run when the callback unwinds
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The promised best-effort stack wipe runs when a callback exits and the process continues, or the contract defines the normal-return boundary.
findings.observed: Both wrappers run the callback before making an ordinary call to the wipe. A callback panic that unwinds skips the wipe. The optimized canary exercise covers normal return.
findings.impact: A consumer that catches panics can retain secret-bearing stack residue. Panic-abort builds already terminate the process. The separate protected-stack thread service has its own cleanup.
findings.recommendedFix: Clear during unwind as well as normal return, or explicitly restrict this wrapper to normal return and direct callers that require unwind cleanup to the appropriate API.
findings.requiredVerification: Check the contract and an unwind-enabled optimized test with a synthetic marker.

findings.title: macOS folder grant is expressed by pathname after the identity check
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The granting contract either retains the checked folder's identity or requires trusted stable ancestors for a path grant.
findings.observed: The constructor holds a directory descriptor and the grant checks identity and emptiness. The sandbox profile then retains only a pathname. It cannot express that held identity against a later directory or ancestor replacement.
findings.impact: The later policy can apply to different storage when another process can replace components of the path. The exact Seatbelt behavior for replacement and links requires native verification.
findings.recommendedFix: Document and enforce an explicit parent-trust and stability condition, or use an object-bound rule. If neither can be verified, keep the path-dependent claim out of the supported grant.
findings.requiredVerification: Confirm native Seatbelt behavior under folder and ancestor replacement and with existing links. Check that intended storage stays within the contract.

findings.title: A synchronized Linux worker can pass clean startup with an unchecked descriptor table
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Admission establishes both whole-process policy and clean startup across the worker contexts allowed to run.
findings.observed: The worker checks the serving thread's descriptor table, then accepts process-wide policy including synchronized or cached reach. A startup sibling can have a separate table. TSYNC does not remove descriptors already open in it. The technical guide documents the census boundary but the worker still reports clean startup.
findings.impact: Where a linked startup library or runtime legitimately starts a sibling with a separate table before serve(), the worker may take secret requests without the documented clean-start condition for the worker as a whole.
findings.recommendedFix: Require an independently established one-thread startup for workers, or inspect each relevant table before admission. Keep the standalone TSYNC decision and worker admission distinct.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify worker admission with and without pre-existing sibling contexts. The passing path must prove both policy scope and startup authority.

findings.title: A child of fork cannot signal itself under the inherited rule
findings.reproduction: Isolate with `signals_to_self_only`, fork, call `kill(getpid(), 0)` in the child.
findings.expected: The documentation says what the child can signal.
findings.observed: The inherited rule names the parent; the child can signal the parent only, and after isolating itself again with the option, no process at all.
findings.impact: A child that relies on `raise` or `abort` fails in a way the documentation did not name.
findings.recommendedFix: Document it.
findings.requiredVerification: A fork test asserts `EACCES` for the child's signal to itself.

findings.title: Windows integrity checks of threads with the hardened access list
findings.reproduction: Enter isolation twice in a process with threads, or start a thread during the call.
findings.expected: `LowIntegrity` reads Confirmed where every thread is low.
findings.observed: A thread opened after it got the hardened list may refuse the token query, reading Unknown; an ended thread's pinned handle stayed in the map.
findings.impact: An honest Unknown where a Confirmed would hold; a handle kept until the call returned.
findings.recommendedFix: Drop an ended thread's handle; reconsider the thread access list.
findings.requiredVerification: A native Windows run of the thread integrity checks.

findings.title: The tracer check accepted a walk cut short
findings.reproduction: A thread ends while `/proc/self/task` is listed, so a traced thread after it is never read.
findings.expected: A walk that missed a thread reports unknown.
findings.observed: The walk counted a thread whose status it could not read, so a short walk passed.
findings.impact: `NoMemoryReading` Confirmed while a thread was traced.
findings.recommendedFix: Count the statuses read; compare with the kernel's count before and after.
findings.requiredVerification: Source review; the tracer roles.

findings.title: The macOS path grant read Confirmed where another user could redirect it
findings.reproduction: A folder made in a group-writable parent, granted, then replaced by another user.
findings.expected: A program can tell before it grants.
findings.observed: The documented example passed `require_process_wide` with `is_private` false.
findings.impact: Secret output can land in another user's folder.
findings.recommendedFix: Check privacy in the example and document the attack.
findings.requiredVerification: A native macOS run of the folder roles.

findings.title: The filter marks of 0.1.1 and 0.2.0 were the same
findings.reproduction: A program holds 0.1.1 through one dependency and 0.2.0 through another; 0.1.1 isolates first.
findings.expected: 0.2.0 never takes 0.1.1's filter for its own.
findings.observed: Both answered the same private marks, so 0.2.0 could skip its own filter and report rules the older one lacks.
findings.impact: Confirmed protections that do not hold in a mixed program.
findings.recommendedFix: Marks of their own for the 0.2 line.
findings.requiredVerification: A test with a filter answering the old marks.

findings.title: The TSYNC check before the layer was not a transaction
findings.reproduction: The filter's TSYNC refused after the check and the layer, by the instruction limit or a thread's new filter.
findings.expected: A stated contract for what a refusal leaves.
findings.observed: The guide promised the filter's TSYNC would go through; each retry added another allowing filter.
findings.impact: An overbroad promise and growing filters.
findings.recommendedFix: State the contract; limit the retries.
findings.requiredVerification: Source review.

findings.title: The worker checked for one thread after its descriptor census
findings.reproduction: A short-lived startup thread opens a descriptor after the census and ends before the count.
findings.expected: One thread is established before the census.
findings.observed: The count came after the census.
findings.impact: A worker admitted with an unchecked descriptor.
findings.recommendedFix: Check the thread count first.
findings.requiredVerification: Source review; the worker suite.

findings.title: macOS privacy ignored volumes mounted to ignore owners
findings.reproduction: A folder made on a volume mounted with `MNT_IGNORE_OWNERSHIP`.
findings.expected: `is_private` false there.
findings.observed: Mode 0700 and no access list read as private although the volume checks no owners.
findings.impact: Secret output in a folder every user can reach.
findings.recommendedFix: Check the mount flag on the folder and above.
findings.requiredVerification: A native macOS run.

findings.title: A remembered TSYNC check went stale across callers
findings.reproduction: After a partial result another thread holds its own filter; a later caller relies on the earlier check.
findings.expected: A layer TSYNC only after a check of that moment.
findings.observed: A success was remembered for the whole process.
findings.impact: Other threads' layers replaced before the filter's TSYNC found the trees apart.
findings.recommendedFix: Use the record only to refuse another try.
findings.requiredVerification: Source review.

findings.title: OpenChannels is a breaking Rust API change under the old package version
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Release versioning reflects changes that invalidate a consumer's existing Rust source.
findings.observed: OpenChannels gained a public field and became non_exhaustive. Previously legal external literals and exhaustive patterns fail here. Cargo.toml still says 0.1.1, the published baseline used for the audit.
findings.impact: Publishing under the existing version cannot represent the changed crate. A patch version would also leave existing semver consumers exposed to the source break.
findings.recommendedFix: Assign a new version. Preserve source compatibility for a compatible increment, or document migration and use the next breaking pre-1.0 series if keeping the type change.
findings.requiredVerification: Build a downstream API compatibility fixture and ensure the package, release tag and changelog agree.

findings.title: The Windows pipe wait skipped the deadline after a put-off client
findings.reproduction: Another process keeps opening the worker's pipe during a timed start.
findings.expected: The start fails at its deadline.
findings.observed: `accept` put the client off and listened again without checking the deadline or the worker.
findings.impact: A start held past its deadline for as long as another process keeps taking the pipe.
findings.recommendedFix: Check both on every turn.
findings.requiredVerification: A native Windows run of the timed start.

findings.title: A mouse report could delete a typed character
findings.reproduction: Mouse tracking in the X10 mode, a click at column or row 95.
findings.expected: A mouse report changes nothing in the line.
findings.observed: Its byte 0x7F was taken for Backspace, which ended the report early and let its last byte into the line.
findings.impact: A secret typed with a stray click is wrong without the user seeing why.
findings.recommendedFix: Take every byte of the report.
findings.requiredVerification: A test types such a report.

findings.title: Release does not run the required optimized stack acceptance on both Linux architectures
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The stack-clear claim is exercised under the actual release profile on Linux x86-64 and ARM64.
findings.observed: The workflow runs cargo test with the test profile. Packaging compiles but does not execute the release suite. The release profile uses different LTO settings. This audit supplies release x86-64 evidence only.
findings.impact: The tag pipeline can pass without validating the compiler-sensitive wipe under the release settings on ARM64.
findings.recommendedFix: Run the focused existing optimized stack acceptance on both Linux architectures as a release prerequisite.
findings.requiredVerification: Record native optimized test runs for both target architectures on the exact release candidate.

findings.title: The documented Linux coverage run fails the stack-clear acceptance test

evidence.level: executed documented coverage recipe and source

findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The documented coverage recipe completes the suite and can produce a measured coverage record for the candidate.
findings.observed: Under the documented LLVM continuous-profile instrumentation, the normal-return stack marker assertion fails: assertion failed: !stack_holds(MARK). The uninstrumented test and release profiles pass the same existing fixture. The test inspects up to twice the intended wipe depth, so this result by itself does not locate residue inside the promised region.
findings.impact: The current source cannot be assigned a fresh full coverage result from the documented procedure. The case also shows the instrumented build is sensitive to frame layout or marker placement.
findings.recommendedFix: Localize the marker relative to the documented wipe window and keep independent acceptance for the optimized uninstrumented build. Make the coverage recipe reproducible and account explicitly for any instrumentation-specific limit.
findings.requiredVerification: Re-run the documented full coverage command and the optimized release stack check. Report the actual LLVM-instrumented result without replacing failed evidence with a previous coverage percentage.

findings.title: dprint failed, and a test failed with inherited descriptors
findings.reproduction: `dprint check`; the isolation suite started with descriptors above 2 open.
findings.expected: Both pass.
findings.observed: A table was not formatted, and the `shared-memory` role expected only descriptors 0 to 2.
findings.impact: Gates fail on an ordinary run.
findings.recommendedFix: Format; take the descriptors open at the role's start.
findings.requiredVerification: `dprint check`; the suite with inherited descriptors.

findings.title: Native platforms and several cases were untested
findings.reproduction: The change set ran on Linux x86-64 only.
findings.expected: Every guarantee has a test on its system.
findings.observed: No native Windows, macOS or ARM64 run; no tests for unwinding, a sibling with a filter of its own, or a speculation role that cannot exercise a refusal.
findings.impact: Defects on other systems stay unseen until a release.
findings.recommendedFix: Add the tests; run CI natively.
findings.requiredVerification: Native CI on the release candidate.

findings.title: Linux without this crate's filter did not build
findings.reproduction: Build for a Linux processor other than x86-64 and AArch64.
findings.expected: The Landlock-only build compiles.
findings.observed: The fallback module lacked `share_filters`.
findings.impact: No build on such processors.
findings.recommendedFix: A conservative fallback.
findings.requiredVerification: A build for such a target.

findings.title: The guide wrongly let a forked child lift the inherited signal rule
findings.reproduction: Fork, isolate again with `signals_to_self_only`, `kill(getpid(), 0)`.
findings.expected: The guide matches the kernel.

findings.title: The stack-clearing contract was stale

findings.title: Linux may exempt a reopened shared secret-memory mapping after fork
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Only secret memory that the current process actually owns is omitted from channel inventory.
findings.observed: Atomic address slots are inherited at fork, while the associated secret mapping is excluded. The exception compares the address and a kernel-supplied name common to memfd_secret mappings.
findings.impact: Under address reuse a continuing child's mapping from another process can be mistaken for an owned allocation. The issue is confined to the own-secret exclusion and continuing child path.
findings.recommendedFix: Use process-specific ownership and backing identity for the exception, or clear ownership inherited from a process that no longer owns the mapping.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify that inherited metadata cannot hide any mapping acquired by the child from elsewhere.

findings.title: The macOS region census treats a general query error as end of enumeration
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: Completion is based on a recognized end of the region walk.
findings.observed: proc_pidinfo returns zero for syscall errors as well as the end condition. The caller breaks for every zero. The ABI landmarks can have been seen before the failure.
findings.impact: A partial walk may be reported complete when the kernel query fails late.
findings.recommendedFix: Distinguish error from the documented end condition and return an incomplete result for other kernel failures.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify behavior on both a normal end and a failed query after the last landmark.

findings.title: Linux file-change filtering leaves an inode-wide write hint mutable
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.
findings.expected: The file-change promise names which inode attributes stay unchanged.
findings.observed: The fcntl filter permits F_SET_RW_HINT. The kernel setter can update the inode's write hint through a read-only descriptor when its ownership check passes.
findings.impact: An inode-level I/O hint can change outside granted directories. No change of file bytes or access mode follows.
findings.recommendedFix: Refuse the inode-wide setter or explicitly narrow the attribute promise.
findings.requiredVerification: Verify the named metadata contract with an ordinary owner-controlled temporary file.

findings.title: Windows size conversions and the label SID went unchecked

findings.title: Descriptor numbers alone do not prove that only trusted channels remain

findings.title: Unix timed startup promises a launch cutoff that the launcher does not enforce
findings.reproduction: Source assessment. Acceptance is a defensive regression for the stated invariant.

remediation.evidence: The filter goes onto other threads only where the layer did, by this call's TSYNC or as recorded for the process, or where the calling thread holds no layer at all. Below ABI 8 both stay on the calling thread and report `Reach::Thread`. Tests: the thread roles on every ABI, and `sibling-then-folders` (folders granted beside a running thread, then `all_threads`: the other thread keeps its sockets).
Linux isolation calls run one at a time (`Entering`), a flag that carries the process's mark, its number and fork count, so a child of `fork` made while another thread held it takes it over.

Before the layer's TSYNC a filter that allows everything goes onto every thread with TSYNC (`seccomp::share_filters`), which the kernel refuses, putting it nowhere, in just that case; the whole call then stays on the calling thread. The layer's TSYNC is tried once per process, right after that check (follow-ups SEC027, SEC031). A call that falls short later leaves other threads more restricted, never less, as the guides say; the option's precondition, no Landlock layer of their own on other threads, is written in the rustdoc and the guides. Test: `foreign-sibling`.

The count of threads is the kernel's own, the `Threads:` line of `/proc/self/status`. `traced` counts only the statuses it read and requires that number to equal the count before and after its walk, else walks again, up to three times, then reports unknown (follow-up SEC018). An atomic view of the threads does not exist, so heavy churn can still make it unknown.

The walk uses `PROC_PIDREGIONPATHINFO`, which returns each region with the file it maps. A writable region that maps a file counts unless it is copy-on-write or empty, whatever its inheritance; names come from the same call.
On macOS `is_private` is false when an access list on the folder or above it allows anything to anyone or cannot be read, and when the volume is mounted to ignore owners (follow-up SEC029).
A failed first discard refuses the reading; the last runs only after a switch that read back, after the mode is restored, and fails the call; the restored mode is read back.

The drain runs only under hidden settings with `VMIN` 0 that read back and must reach the end of the waiting input; the original settings, speeds included, are read back after the restore; each failure is an error, and the restore's error wins. `fcntl` failure refuses the descriptor, and an unknown device matches nothing.

A guard clears when the frame is left, by return or unwinding; the work runs below a 2 KiB cushion of unwritten stack, so the clearing starts above its frames; zeros are written once, in place; WebAssembly clears nothing. Tests mark the work, the closure's own locals and a panicking work.

On macOS `is_private` is false when a folder above, up to the root, belongs to someone other than the user or root, lets its group or others write without the sticky bit, carries an access list that allows anything to anyone, or lies on a volume mounted to ignore owners. The grant stays by path, as the guides and `SECURITY.md` say; the example checks `is_private` before granting.
A worker isolates itself without `all_threads` and, on Linux, is unclean unless it has one thread, by the kernel's count, checked before its descriptor census (follow-up SEC028).
The option's row says that the child cannot lift the inherited rule and what it can signal before and after isolating itself; the fork test asserts `EACCES`.

An ended thread's pinned handle is dropped at once, and the branch that could no longer run went with it. The access list is not widened: every process of the user would get the right, and a refused query reads Unknown, never Confirmed.
Only the statuses read count; the walk must equal the kernel's count before and after, else it runs again, up to three times, then reports unknown.
The example checks `is_private` before granting, and `SECURITY.md` describes the redirection; `is_private` covers the folders above (SEC009).
The 0.2 line answers its own marks; the `old-marks` test installs a filter answering 0.1's and finds that 0.2 puts in its own.
The guides state that a call falling short leaves other threads more restricted, never less; the allowing filter goes in once at most (SEC031).
The count comes first, then the census, then the worker's own streams.
`is_private` is false when the folder or one above lies on such a volume, or `fstatfs` fails.
The layer's TSYNC is tried once per process, right after its own check; later calls that would need it stay on the calling thread, and the rustdoc says so.
The version is 0.2.0 in `Cargo.toml` and both lockfiles, and the changelog opens with the breaking changes.
Every turn of the loop checks the worker and the deadline first.
Every byte of a mouse report from 0x20 up, DEL included, belongs to it; a byte below ends it and counts, so Enter is never swallowed. A test types the report.
CI runs `cargo test --release --lib stack::` on Linux x86-64 and ARM64, and a release runs CI first.

The test passes the word's complement and makes the word only after the reading. Under continuous profiling the `shared-memory` check leaves the profile file's mapping out. The documented recipe passes all checks; `docs/COVERAGE.md` and the README give its result.
The guide is formatted, and the role takes the descriptors open at its start as expected.

Tests for the closure's locals, unwinding, a sibling with its own filter, folders beside a running thread, the 0.1 marks and the child's signals; the speculation role says when it cannot check. Native runs follow the push.
The fallback answers false, and the layer stays on the calling thread there.
Corrected; the fork test asserts `EACCES` (SEC015).
The guides and the rustdoc state unwinding, the 2 KiB cushion, the free stack needed, captures and returns, panic-abort builds and WebAssembly.
The slots belong to the process that wrote them, by a mark of its number and fork count; a child empties them before it names itself their owner (follow-ups SEC025, SEC030).
Only `EINVAL`, no region at or after the address, ends the walk; any other error leaves the inventory incomplete.
The filter refuses both whenever it refuses file changes.
Sizes go through `isize::try_from`, and the SID must be non-null and pass `IsValidSid`.
The count is gone: a filter that allows everything goes onto every thread with TSYNC first, which the kernel refuses in exactly the divergent case (SEC002, SEC031).

grants.name: Linux writable folders
grants.admits: New, empty, held folders granted by a first Landlock layer; the filter lets new files, folders, links, renames and removals through where Landlock decides

grants.name: macOS writable folders
grants.admits: Sandbox rules by path; another user may redirect the path where `is_private` is false

grants.name: `Options::all_threads` (TSYNC)
grants.admits: The caller's layer replaces other threads' layers once per process, after a kernel check of their filters; a call that falls short leaves them more restricted, never less

grants.name: Existing descriptors and shared memory
grants.admits: Whatever the program named in `only`; channels of other threads' own tables

grants.name: Hidden terminal input
grants.admits: The terminal's settings changed while reading, restored and read back; up to 64 KiB of waiting input dropped

grants.name: Windows console input
grants.admits: Echo and line editing off while reading; the prompt on a console the process may write to

grants.name: Unix worker pipes and executable
grants.admits: Kernel pipe copies; a worker with one thread at its start, checked before its descriptors

grants.name: Windows worker IPC and recovery
grants.admits: Local clients that contend for the pipe are put off, within the deadline

grants.name: Optional reports
grants.admits: Private marks of the 0.2 line; a cooperative host's filter can still imitate them

grants.name: Stack and secret copies
grants.admits: Frames above the cleared window, registers, captures and returns; nothing cleared on WebAssembly
